channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: US Treasury yields reached multi-year highs on 28 September, with the 10-year at 5.241%, the highest since June 2007, and the 30-year at 5.561%, the highest since June 2002, according to MarketScreener.
item.description:
The two-year yield reached 4.922%, its highest since May 2024. Milano Finanza attributes the pressure on bond markets to the prolonged war with Iran and its effect on energy prices, concerns about the sustainability of public finances, and a large volume of AI-related debt. The Globe and Mail notes that the Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September for the first time in three years in response to energy-price inflation after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, that markets expect further rises, and that 30-year US mortgage rates now exceed 7%. Emerging-market investors, including Aegon USA Investment Management and JPMorgan Asset Management, are pulling back from their riskiest bond positions, according to The Economic Times, with credit spreads at their tightest since 2007. Levels and historical comparisons differ between outlets and sessions; this brief uses the MarketScreener figures. The reporting does not give euro-area yields for the same day.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading, long-term borrowing costs are where rates meet construction: mortgage rates above 7% work against US housing demand, and higher long yields raise the financing cost of industrial and infrastructure projects. The highs reach furthest back at the long end (30-year since June 2002, 10-year since June 2007, two-year only since May 2024), which on a general reading reflects concerns about inflation and public debt more than the Federal Reserve's own rate. For adhesive technologies, the exposure runs through US residential construction and through customers' capital spending decisions, on a general reading. Points that may be worth considering include how US construction customers are reporting order intake at current mortgage rates, and how financing costs affect planned capacity investments in the region.

MarketScreener | The Globe and Mail | Milano Finanza | The Economic Times

item.title: Total profits of China's industrial enterprises above designated size rose 15.7% year on year to CNY 5.27 trillion in the first eight months of 2026, the National Bureau of Statistics reports, slowing from 17.6% in the first seven months.
item.description:
High-tech manufacturing above designated size posted profit growth of 54.7%, 39 percentage points above all industrial enterprises above designated size. The electronics industry recorded a 1.1-fold year-on-year increase in profits, as reported, and contributed 62% of the profit growth of all industrial enterprises above designated size, according to Chinatimes. The reporting does not give the August month on its own, profits for the chemical industry or for construction materials, or revenue figures.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Growth is concentrated: with electronics providing 62% of the profit increase, the remaining 38% came from all other industries together, so, on a general reading, the headline rate overstates how broad the profit growth is. The slowdown from 17.6% to 15.7% in the cumulative rate means August's year-on-year profit growth was below the 17.6% January–July rate. On a general reading, electronics assembly is a user of specialised adhesives, encapsulants and thermal materials, so the segment driving China's industrial profits is one that adhesive technologies serve directly, while profit growth in other industries may be weaker than the headline suggests. Points that may be worth considering include how electronics-related demand in China compares with other industrial segments in the order book, and whether the slowdown in the cumulative rate continues in September.

Chinatimes

item.title: Switzerland's Federal Council plans to sign an expanded free trade agreement with China in autumn 2026, with the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs estimating additional savings of around CHF 244 million a year.
item.description:
The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Seco) puts the additional savings potential at about CHF 244 million, or about EUR 258 million, a year, according to Handelsblatt. The report places the agreement against a problem Swiss and German mechanical engineers share in China: Chinese manufacturers increasingly produce and supply goods that used to come from Europe. The reporting does not give a signing date, the tariff lines or sectors covered, whether the savings accrue to Swiss exporters, importers or both, or when the expanded agreement would take effect.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The planned agreement shows a non-EU European economy seeking to deepen trade preferences with China while the EU and several member states, on a general reading, are moving towards more trade defence against Chinese imports. The report names machinery as the sector facing Chinese competition. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, mechanical engineering is a customer segment for industrial adhesives, sealants and threadlockers, and a shift in where machines for the Chinese market are built changes where that demand sits. Points that may be worth considering include whether Swiss-made goods containing European inputs would gain preferential access to China under the expanded rules of origin, once published, and how that compares with EU exporters' access.

Handelsblatt

item.title: China's LNG imports are expected to fall to 63 million tonnes in 2026, from 66 million in 2025 and a peak of 79 million in 2021, according to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis, and Chinese buyers are also reselling cargoes abroad.
item.description:
The IEEFA estimates China's total LNG resales in 2025 at 17 to 19 million tonnes, with South Korea, Japan and the Netherlands as the leading destinations. Chinese buyers signed almost 60 million tonnes of new long-term LNG supply contracts between 2021 and 2023, more than the total contracted in the previous decade, according to the report carried by Anadolu Agency. The reporting does not give 2026 resale volumes, any profit figure beyond the headline, or the prices at which cargoes were resold.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The finding shows China reselling a share of its LNG as well as importing it, at a time when the Iran war has disrupted Middle East energy flows. The Netherlands appearing among the top destinations means some LNG delivered into Europe was resold by Chinese buyers. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, this makes European gas prices partly dependent on how Chinese buyers use their contract flexibility, which in turn depends on China's own demand. Gas is, on a general reading, both a site energy cost and a feedstock for many chemical raw materials, so this reaches adhesive technologies through European gas-linked costs. Points that may be worth considering include how the European gas supply picture for the winter treats volumes resold from Asian contracts, and whether a rise in China's domestic gas demand would reduce those resales.

Anadolu Agency

item.title: New housing supply in India's top seven cities rose 18% in the third quarter of 2026, according to Anarock, while a separate report puts first-half primary sales in tier-1 cities flat by value at about INR 3.63 lakh crore.
item.description:
Anarock reports that new supply rose 120% in Hyderabad, 27% in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and 17% in Bengaluru, while most other cities saw new supply decline year on year; the MMR and Bengaluru accounted for 48% of sales across the seven cities. The September India Housing Report by CRE Matrix and the National Association of Realtors–India finds primary housing sales in tier-1 cities of about INR 3.63 lakh crore in the first half, virtually unchanged from the record first half of 2025, while the number of homes sold fell about 2% to 258,000 and developers launched nearly 298,000 units, up 7%. The two reports cover different city sets and periods and are not combined here. The reporting does not give Anarock's third-quarter sales volumes or unsold inventory.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The same CRE Matrix report shows launches of about 298,000 units against 258,000 sold in the first half, so supply rose faster than unit sales; stable value with fewer units points to a higher average ticket rather than broader demand. The third-quarter supply rise is concentrated in three cities. On a general reading, new launches turn into construction and finishing work over the following years, which is where tile adhesives, waterproofing and sealants are used; the gap between launches and unit sales is the risk to that pipeline. Points that may be worth considering include which of the high-growth cities are served directly by the distribution network, and whether developers in the cities with declining supply are slowing projects already launched.

The Hindu BusinessLine | Business Standard

item.title: Thailand produced 124,646 cars in August 2026, up 10.93% from a year earlier, according to the Federation of Thai Industries, with domestic sales up 25.59% while exports fell 2.04%.
item.description:
The export decline in August compares with a rise of 2.39% the month before. The figures are from the Federation of Thai Industries (FTI), which on 28 September also said, through Surapong Paisitpatanapong, adviser to the president of its Automotive Industry Club, that the automotive supply chain has not yet been affected by the severe floods of the previous weekend and that the floods are not expected to affect car production. The reporting does not give year-to-date production, the split between passenger cars, pickups and electric vehicles, the reason for the jump in domestic sales, or the base month's level, so it does not show whether August 2025 was unusually weak. The FTI's flood statement is an assessment made while flooding was still being reported in eastern Bangkok.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Thailand is, on a general reading, the main vehicle production hub of Southeast Asia and a large pickup exporter, so the combination of a strong domestic market and weaker exports matters for suppliers that serve both. On a general reading, a rise in domestic sales depends on domestic credit and incentives rather than on export demand. Vehicle production draws on structural bonding, sealing, and interior and body adhesives on a general reading, so monthly assembly figures are one of the closer demand indicators for adhesive technologies in the region. Points that may be worth considering include whether the domestic sales rise continues into September, and whether the flood situation changes the FTI's assessment for plants and suppliers around Bangkok.

MarketScreener | Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: A State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang on 28 September proposed studying and introducing measures to stabilise China's real estate market, as Beijing and Shanghai announced rules reforming commercial housing sales.
item.description:
The State Council executive meeting also proposed stronger counter-cyclical adjustment of macro policy, measures to promote employment and income growth, and reserve policies to boost domestic demand; it heard a report on progress in controlling new pollutants. No measures, amounts or dates for the property package are given. The city rules are more specific. Beijing's housing commission and three other departments announced implementation opinions on 24 September proposing to comprehensively strengthen the management of pre-sales: for projects whose land-transfer announcement came after 28 August 2026, the main structure of each building must be topped out before a pre-sale application. Beijing also introduced a lead-bank system under which developers open capital accounts with a lead bank where all relevant project funds are uniformly managed, including development loans, developers' own funds and proceeds from selling completed homes. The rules in both cities cover supervision of pre-sale funds, promotion of sales of completed homes, real-estate financing and land supply, according to Commercial Times. The reporting does not describe Shanghai's rules in detail or give current sales or price figures.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The two layers work differently. The State Council statement is a signal of support still to be defined; Beijing's rules change how new projects are financed, by moving pre-sales later in the construction cycle for land announced after 28 August and placing project funds with a lead bank. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a topping-out requirement before pre-sale means developers must finance more of the structure before receiving buyers' money, which can slow new starts at weaker developers while making completion of started projects more likely. On a general reading, demand for adhesive technologies in China from interior finishing and flooring follows completions more than starts. Points that may be worth considering include whether the State Council's measures, once published, address financing for completion, and how the Beijing and Shanghai rules shift the timing of finishing work in the two cities.

Commercial Times | Commercial Times

item.title: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on a visit to Dillinger Hütte that Germany needs its own steel industry in the future, as Saarland's steelmakers convert to hydrogen-based production at a cost of about EUR 4.6 billion.
item.description:
Merz visited the Dillinger Hütte construction site in Saarland on 28 September to be briefed on the conversion of the Saar steel industry to more climate-friendly production, in which steel will be made with hydrogen rather than coal. Dillinger and Saarstahl are investing around EUR 4.6 billion; the federal and state governments are funding EUR 2.6 billion and the companies pay the rest, according to WiWo, Süddeutsche Zeitung and Tagesschau (one Süddeutsche Zeitung report gives nearly EUR 5 billion). Merz said he sees the transformation towards green steel as being on the right track. Thyssenkrupp in Duisburg and Salzgitter in Lower Saxony are working on their own conversion projects. Tagesschau, reporting ahead of the visit, adds a risk: the European Commission presented plans a few months ago under which the price of emission certificates would rise more slowly than planned, and the Saarland steel industry sees the planned conversion in danger because a possible reform of the EU emissions trading system could make it uneconomical. The reporting does not give Merz's response to that concern, a timetable for the first hydrogen-based output, or where the hydrogen will come from.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The statement is political support for a domestic steel base, not a new measure: the public funding had already been reported before the visit, and the open question is the carbon price that makes hydrogen-based steel pay. The Tagesschau point is the load-bearing one: on a general reading, if certificate prices rise more slowly, the cost gap between coal-based and hydrogen-based steel stays wider for longer. On a general reading, German steel producers and their customers in automotive, construction and machinery are important users of metal surface treatment, coatings and structural bonding, so the pace of the conversion affects a customer base of adhesive technologies in Germany. Points that may be worth considering include how the German steel customers in the portfolio are planning for lower-carbon steel grades, and whether new steel grades or surfaces would require requalification of pretreatment or bonding products.

Süddeutsche Zeitung | WiWo | Süddeutsche Zeitung | Tagesschau

item.title: The UK government plans a "Your First Home" scheme under which first-time buyers in England can buy a new-build home with a minimum 2.5% deposit and an equity loan, with the details to be set in next month's budget.
item.description:
Shares in UK housebuilders rose on 28 September after the government said it would confirm the new equity loan programme in next month's budget: Barratt Redrow rose 14%, and Vistry, Persimmon, Taylor Wimpey and Bellway were up between 14% and 16%, according to The Guardian, which says the scheme was announced by Andy Burnham. MarketScreener reports that the government will provide loans of up to 20% of a property's value, letting buyers who can afford mortgage payments but have struggled to save a deposit qualify for mortgages that would otherwise need larger deposits; The Guardian describes a 20% equity loan. The scheme revives a policy type that ended in March 2023 with the previous "Help to Buy" programme, since when sales have languished, according to MarketScreener. Investors and analysts quoted there say much depends on the budget, which will set out who qualifies and where the support can be used. The reporting does not give the budget date, the scheme's total cost, the number of homes it is expected to support, or any regional or price caps.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The scheme is tied to new-build homes, so, on a general reading, its effect runs through construction volumes rather than through transactions in existing homes; the housebuilder share moves are consistent with that. It is an announcement, not yet a measured change in demand: the qualifying rules in the budget decide how many buyers can use it. On a general reading, new-build residential construction draws on the full range of construction adhesives, sealants, flooring and tile adhesives and insulation bonding, so a sustained rise in UK housing starts would reach adhesive technologies through distributors and contractors. Points that may be worth considering include how UK construction channel partners plan stock ahead of the budget, and which product lines in new-build residential work would respond first if starts rise.

The Guardian | MarketScreener | MarketScreener

item.title: India's Supreme Court reserved judgement on 28 September in the case on front-of-pack labelling regulations for packaged food, and food companies have asked for the red colour of the regulator's proposed hexagon warning to be reconsidered.
item.description:
The court directed all parties to file final written submissions within three days. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had earlier told the court that it proposes red hexagon warning labels with a white square on the front of the pack, drawing on the format adopted by Canada; the system is meant to mark packaged items high in salt, sugar or fat. The All India Food Processors Association, which represents dozens of Indian and foreign food companies, argues that consumers associate red with the mandatory non-vegetarian mark and that a second prominent red symbol could confuse them. The proposal follows a heated public debate on the lack of such labels and comes despite a multi-year industry campaign against them. Milind Deora, chairman of the parliamentary committee on subordinate legislation, says six months to a year is enough for food companies to switch; the FSSAI had proposed, during the court case, about four months to finalise the regulations, including consultation, followed by a 365-day transition. The reporting does not give the nutrient thresholds, the number of products affected, or when the judgement is expected.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The judgement could shape the format and, with the regulations that follow, the timetable for a change that would touch the front of every affected package in what Asharq Al-Awsat calls a more than USD 100 billion industry. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a mandatory front-of-pack change works in two ways on packaging: a wave of artwork and label changes within the transition, and reformulation by brands that want to stay below the thresholds and avoid the warning. On a general reading, labels, flexible laminates and folding cartons for packaged food use label, lamination and carton-sealing adhesives, so the transition could bring a burst of relabelling and repackaging work for packaging adhesive technologies in India rather than a lasting change in volume. Points that may be worth considering include how packaging converters serving Indian food brands plan for a label change within the proposed 365-day window, and whether a format drawn from Canada's makes design work from other markets reusable.

The Hindu BusinessLine | The Hindu BusinessLine | MarketScreener | LiveMint | The Economic Times | Asharq Al-Awsat

item.title: Brent crude futures rose for a second session to USD 105.91 a barrel on 29 September, as concern over Middle East supply outweighed preliminary Kpler data showing crude exports from major Middle East producers at their highest since February.
item.description:
The 28 September move followed President Trump's rejection of an Iranian peace proposal: Brent was up USD 1.68, or 1.6%, at USD 106 a barrel by 13:20 GMT, an intraday level (the reporting gives no settlement price for 28 September), after reaching its highest level since 15 September earlier in the session, according to The Standard. Preliminary figures from the data provider Kpler show crude exports from major Middle East producers at 12.8 million barrels a day in September, the highest since February, helped by increased shipments from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. ANZ Research analysts describe the US–Iran ceasefire talks as deadlocked, and oil gains eased after Saudi Arabia resumed exports through its East-West pipeline, with flows of 3.5 million barrels a day. Commerzbank Research sees the collapse of diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as the dominant driver of prices. The IEA estimates that average daily transit through the Strait was about 7.6 million barrels in August, a significant decrease from before the conflict (no pre-conflict figure is given), and Commercial Times describes a tight market in which near-month prices are above later months, with declining global inventories. Other outlets quoted intraday levels for 28 September that differ widely; they are not used here. The reporting does not give a pre-war figure for Middle East exports to compare with the 12.8 million.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The two measures point in different directions: preliminary data show more crude leaving major Middle East producers, but the price keeps rising because the market prices the risk that the Strait stays closed. A market where near-month prices are above later months, on a general reading, rewards supply available now over supply later, which can matter for how term-contract and spot purchases are priced. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, crude-derived petrochemicals such as solvents, resins and polymer raw materials follow crude with a lag, and that lag is where adhesive technologies meet this price. Points that may be worth considering include the share of oil-derived raw materials bought on contract against spot, and how quickly price formulas in supplier contracts pass a sustained Brent level above USD 100 through.

The Economic Times | CNA | MarketScreener | Commercial Times | The Standard

item.title: A potentially stricter classification of talc could prompt coatings manufacturers to reconsider its use, according to Akzo Nobel, DAW, Diessner and Vitex, as reported by European Coatings, with Vitex referring to a possible Carc. 1B reclassification.
item.description:
Talc is used as a multifunctional ingredient in many formulations, according to the report, and plays an important role in meeting specific technical performance requirements. Aristotelis Nikolakopoulos, R&D Director at Vitex, said a potential reclassification of talc as Carc. 1B would have a significant impact on the company's product portfolio, because talc is widely used as a functional filler across its decorative, marine and industrial coatings, including paints, varnishes, primers, putties, roadmaking and specialty products. The report is about how manufacturers would respond to a classification that has not been decided. It does not say which authority is examining the classification, at what stage the process is, or when a decision could come. It also does not name the alternative fillers the manufacturers are considering, give the share of their formulations that contain talc, or say what the other three companies expect for their own portfolios.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a Category 1B carcinogen classification under the EU's hazard-classification rules carries labelling duties and restrictions on some uses for mixtures above concentration limits, which is why formulators look at substitution before a decision rather than after. Also on a general reading, talc is used as a filler and rheology aid in adhesive and sealant formulations, not only in paints, so the question the four coatings companies describe is likely to reach formulators of adhesive technologies in the same way. On a general reading, a substitution affects performance, qualification with customers and supply of the replacement filler at the same time. Points that may be worth considering include which products in the portfolio contain talc above the relevant concentration limits, how long requalification of an alternative filler would take with key customers, and whether suppliers of alternative fillers have the capacity for a shift across the industry.

European Coatings
